Name: Commodore Amiga
Note: IPF playback needs a compatible CAPSIMG library and Kickstart BIOS.

Name: Commodore 64
Note: NIB/NBZ convert to G64. G64, TAP and T64 keep their bytes. Tape-side swapping is checked separately from disk playlists.

Name: Sony PlayStation
Note: CHDs stay loose. CUE files keep their referenced tracks and matching SBI files.

Name: Sega CD / Mega-CD
Note: The current Onion PicoDrive build supports relative-path M3U playlists and disk swapping. CUE/ISO/CHD media are kept loose in .hidden.

Name: Amstrad CPC
Note: Playlist unsupported with the default CrocoDS core: no M3U disk-swap interface.
DefaultReason: Playlist unsupported with the default CrocoDS core: no M3U disk-swap interface.

Name: MSX / MSX2
Note: The default blueMSX core supports disk playlists; its Databases and Machines BIOS folders are required.

Name: Commodore VIC-20
Note: For actual disk images. Cartridge and PRG files are not grouped as disks.

Name: PC Engine CD / TurboGrafx-CD
Note: Playlist unsupported with Beetle PCE Fast: M3U loading exists, but in-game Disk Control is unavailable.
DefaultReason: Playlist unsupported with Beetle PCE Fast: M3U loading exists, but in-game Disk Control is unavailable.

Name: MS-DOS
Note: Disk-image sets only. Installation and game startup may still be required inside DOSBox.

Name: ZX Spectrum
Note: Playlist unsupported with the inspected default Onion Fuse build: M3U loading is unavailable. ZX IPF-to-DSK conversion remains available in menu Z.
DefaultReason: Playlist unsupported with the inspected default Onion Fuse build: M3U loading is unavailable. ZX IPF-to-DSK conversion remains available in menu Z.
